Input, Process, and Output
Most programs can be broken into three main parts:
input, process, and output.
Input is information that enters the program,
process is what the program does with that
information, and output is the result produced.
This is called the Input-Process-Output (IPO)
Model.

Planning with IPO Charts
An IPO Chart identifies what information a program needs, what it will do with that information, and what result it
will produce.
IPO charts help organize a program before any code is written.
Each section describes the purpose of that stage rather than the exact Python syntax.

IPO Wrap Up
Python programs commonly follow the Input-Process-
Output (IPO) model.
input() collects information from the user and always
returns that information as a string, so numeric input may
need to be cast with int() or float().
print() displays output, and values can be combined using
commas, concatenation, or f-strings, with f-strings usually
providing the clearest formatting.
Escape sequences such as \n and \" can also be used to
control how strings are displayed.
